clusters.title: Reinforcing an objective we already hold instead of using the unit where it scores more
clusters.hint: The AI sends a unit to reinforce an objective it already holds (pass-2 'reinforcing it (we hold with OC N, enemy can bring ~M)') when a forward objective, a table quarter or a kill elsewhere is worth more. At s7437 r2 the Allarus hold obj_center with OC 6; COORD-5 counts ~7 enemy OC one move away and asks for 2 more OC, so pass 2 sends Custodian Guard Beta to the centre at its full hold value (48.2) instead of Advancing to obj_nml_2 (30.7). Forcing Beta -> obj_nml_2 (Advance) measured +4.36 over 36 seeds in one-round rollouts and +19.0 [3.3, 34.7] over 12 full games. ROUND 3 TRIED a fix (REINFORCE-CAP: price the reinforcement as insurance = hold terms x the chance the enemy brings enough OC, when no single projected enemy unit can contest alone) and DROPPED it after review: (1) COORD-5's projection counts only units whose centroid is within M+2"+range; Gretchin (10 OC, 11.4") and Lootas (10 OC, 9.9") could each take the 6-OC centre with an average Advance, and the Ork AI put Gretchin on the centre in 3 of 4 fix replays (secured it in one) - the cap fired only through that blind spot; (2) the holders (Allarus) declared charges off the centre in 4 of 4 replays (CH-LEAVE only halves the score), so 'held' overstated the OC that stays; (3) the gain came from table quarters under Reconnaissance Sweep (Beta Advancing reached a quarter; walking there measured -4.0), plus kills and denial - the cap ignored cards. Also found: RACE-1's long-trip Advance test and _should_unit_advance ignore [ASSAULT] (Beta's Guardian Spear is [ASSAULT], so Advancing costs it no shooting). The round-3 patch and both reviews are in tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/reinforce_insurance/ (round3_attempt.patch, round3_reviews.json): read them first and do not repeat the dropped design. Directions the reviewer suggested: an [ASSAULT]-aware Advance rules fix; valuing an uncovered table quarter for quarter-scoring cards (Reconnaissance Sweep primary, Engage on All Fronts secondary) near its VP; a threat model that uses Advance reach and leaves out holders that will charge off. Guardrail s7418 r3 p2 shows holding the centre INSTEAD of attacking out was harmful (-8.33): do not fix this by vetoing the holders' charges.

clusters.title: The sole keeper of a safe home objective still stays put where V9's release does not fire (Custodes mirror)
clusters.hint: V9 (5e70bc2) has KEEPER-RELEASE (FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE=1, _keeper_release_check / _keeper_release_threat / _keeper_release_primary_counts in AIDecisionMaker.gd): the sole keeper of OUR HOME objective leaves only if it is not fragile, its best other candidate beats holding by KEEPER_RELEASE_MIN_GAIN (5), our primary pays nothing for home, no enemy model can be in range by the end of the enemy's next turn (on-board: M + 12" + 6" (+6" if it may advance and charge) to the objective's range/hosting area; reserves that can arrive), and another unit can step back onto home in one move and is not sent elsewhere by pass 2. It made the measured move at s7437 (Custodes vs Orks, +7.30 n36) but it NEVER fires in the Custodes mirror: the round-3 bench had 42/42 identical V9-vs-V7D pairs there (reviewers: the nearest enemy is 23.4" from the home area vs a 24" reach for M6). Round 4 found the same mistake exactly there: s7453 (P2, round 1) and s7454 (P1, round 1), Custodian Guard kept as 'sole holder' of home; moving it to obj_center measured +6.17 and +4.83 (36 seeds each). In both, the decider's card is Take and Hold. First find WHICH V9 condition blocks each release (threat reach margin? the card counting home? the backup? the margin?) by replaying with the V9 code and reading the [KEEPER_RELEASE] lines. Then widen only what the evidence supports (for example a realistic reach model instead of the max-roll worst case, or how a hold rule that counts home is valued in round 1), keep s7437 releasing, and respect the guardrails: at s7451 (Custodes mirror, P2, round 1) keeping hold was RIGHT (-4.33), at s7420 leaving was harmful (-2.00), and fragile keepers stay. A separate revision is changing the Advance->Normal-move conversion block after pass 2 (record/pace); do not edit that block. Use the new param FIX_KEEPER_REACH for your change (FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE stays as is).

clusters.title: A lone unit is sent to flip an objective the enemy holds with far more OC, while a winnable objective is dropped as 'already taken'
clusters.hint: At s7454 r3 (Custodes mirror, P2) Custodian Guard Gamma (3 models) was sent to flip obj_nml_1, which the enemy holds with OC 14 ('needs 6 more OC after this unit'); Advancing to obj_center instead measured +21.50 [16.93, 26.07] over 36 seeds. The critic: the centre (~20 VP) was dropped as 'already taken' although the friendly unit heading there (Beta) was still 9" away; count a unit as taking an objective only when it is in range now; reject or heavily penalise an objective where enemy OC in range exceeds the unit's OC plus allies that can arrive. Read the decision record first: which pass made this choice (capture, attack conversion, support), why obj_center's need was 0, and how the flip was scored. LESSON: round 2's FIX_FAR_TRIP (skip 2+-turn trips the race says are lost) passed every gate and still lost 6.26 VP per game in the Custodes mirror (units held back scored less on secondary cards), and FIX_OVERCOMMIT gave no gain; both are off. Do not build a broad trip or race veto. Guardrails where the AI's own (flip / supporting) move was RIGHT: s7455 r3 (-15.0), s7431 r3 (-6.83); several flip moves measured neutral (s7458 r1, s7455 r2 / r3, s7457 r3, s7452 r2). Use the param FIX_LONE_FLIP. UPDATE 18:40: s7455 r2 p1 movement_2_4 (Beta moves toward obj_nml_1 / a charge target to flip an OC 11 hold; alternative Normal move to obj_center) was a guardrail at 12 seeds (+8.0, neutral) and is now CONFIRMED at 36 seeds (+5.92 [1.30, 10.53]): it is a second finding in the same direction as s7454 r3.

clusters.title: Declaring a low-odds charge (17-28%) whose expected gain is smaller than what the charge costs
clusters.hint: Two round-2 charges in the Custodes vs Orks fixture were worse than not charging over 36 seeds: s7469 r2 P2 Stormboyz (140 pts) declare a 28% charge (8.5 in) at Blade Champion Alpha (T7, 2+ save, 4+ invulnerable, on an objective) with 'expected 8.9 melee dmg vs 7 HP' (+4.33 [1.37, 7.30] for no charge), and s7467 r2 P1 Allarus Custodians (270 pts) declare a 17% charge (9.9 in) at a 4-wound Mek (+2.64 [0.40, 4.88]). The critic notes repeat across rounds: expected melee damage overstated against 2+/4++ targets, the failure and overwatch cost understated, bonus terms (order_round_aggression, kill/objective bonuses) lifting a charge above the AI's own odds threshold. In 11e a failed charge does not move the unit (core rules), so the cost of a failed charge is overwatch (Fire Overwatch) and what else the unit gives up, and the cost of a successful one includes the fight back and being locked in combat (and CH-LEAVE when it leaves an objective). Round 1's FIX_CHARGE_EV (gang-up bonus counts only real help) is OFF since the round-1 bundle test; round 3's low-odds charge finding faded with more seeds. IMPORTANT: low odds alone are not the cause. Guardrails where the AI's own charge was right: s7431 r3 Allarus 28% at Blade Champion Alpha (-5.00 [-9.22, -0.78], harmful), s7403 r3 Battlewagon 42% (-3.67 harmful); s7431 r2 Allarus 17% (-5.08 neutral), s7433 r2 Allarus 28% (-3.17 neutral), s7408 r3 Stormboyz (-5.08 neutral) lean the same way. Find what separates the findings from these (damage model, target value, what the charger leaves, what the target does next) before you design. Re-check running (pr8, 24 seeds): s7454 r2 Delta 28% at Blade Champion Beta (+5.42 n12), s7457 r2 Prosecutors 8% (+4.50 n12); their cases are in 40k/tests/rollout_cases/pr8/. UPDATE 18:40: the pr8 re-check CONFIRMED s7457 r2 Prosecutors 8% charge -> no charge (+3.81 [0.20, 7.41], 36 seeds; now a finding) and did NOT confirm s7454 r2 Delta 28% at Blade Champion Beta (+2.44 [-1.43, 6.32], 36 seeds; now a neutral guardrail).

clusters.title: A unit is spent on a screen position (backfield gap / deep-strike denial) while an objective nobody holds is within reach
clusters.hint: s7467 r1 P2 (Orks vs Custodes): Gretchin are sent to screen a 'backfield gap' at (1600,1520) near obj_nml_2, but the plan does not take obj_nml_2, which nobody holds; Advancing the Gretchin onto obj_nml_2 measured +3.64 [1.82, 5.46] over 36 seeds. Screens are chosen in the movement planner's screening step (roles: backfield gap, deny deep strike near a home objective, screening valuable friendlies, block an approaching enemy unit) after objective assignment; check how a screen's flat score compares with the objective value the unit gives up, and whether objectives that need no fight (uncontrolled, no enemy near) are offered to screen-role units at all. 22 measured screen positions exist (tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/measured_positions.json, search 'screen'): most are neutral and point both ways. Same direction (objective better, not significant): s7456 r1 Prosecutors deep-strike screen vs obj_home_2 (+3.25), s7438 r1 Prosecutors vs obj_nml_1 (+2.42), s7451 r1 Prosecutors vs obj_nml_1 (+1.58), s7474 r1 Gretchin backfield gap vs obj_nml_1 (+1.50). Opposite direction (the screen was right): s7408 r1 Burna Boyz B 'screening valuable friendlies' vs Normal move to obj_center (-5.83 [-10.75, -0.92], harmful), s7437 r1 Burna backfield gap vs Advance obj_center (-3.25), s7408 r1 Burna backfield gap (-2.83), s7423 r1 Gretchin backfield gap vs obj_nml_1 (-2.25). Find what separates the finding from the opposite-direction positions (is the objective empty and uncontested? can the unit hold it? does the screen protect something that matters, e.g. against deep strike or a charge?) before you design. Only one finding is confirmed: keep the trigger narrow.

clusters.title: Ork units are treated as able to charge after Advancing on every turn (the Waaagh! rule text is misread), so melee units Advance 'to attack' and lose the charge
clusters.hint: Two Ork melee units Advanced 'to attack' when a Normal move would have reached charge range, and could then not charge: s7468 r3 P2 Stormboyz 'advances to attack Prosecutor Squad (12.0 in away - closing to charge range (0.0 in after move))' vs a Normal move to obj_nml_1: +6.14 [3.08, 9.19] over 36 seeds (CONFIRMED); s7473 r3 P1 Beast Snagga Boyz 'advances to attack Allarus Custodians (9.5 in - closing to charge range (3.5 in after move))' vs a Normal move onto obj_center: +11.25 [5.09, 17.41] over 12 seeds (24-seed re-check pr9 running); s7472 r3 P1 Beast Snagga Boyz the same pattern: +2.00 [-4.12, 8.12] (12 seeds, same direction). LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (verify it, do not take it on trust): the melee chase gate in AIDecisionMaker.gd (~line 2643, 'Advance vs normal move') sets can_advance_and_charge_flag from flags.effect_advance_and_charge OR AIAbilityAnalyzerData.unit_has_ability_containing(unit, 'advance') AND ...(unit, 'charge'); with that flag it always Advances. EVERY unit in 40k/armies/Orks_2000.json has the army ability 'Waaagh!' whose description contains both words ('...that advance move does not prevent that unit from being eligible to declare a charge' - but only WHILE the unit is riled up, i.e. for one turn after the once-per-battle War Cry). The game itself sets flags.effect_advance_and_charge while the Waaagh! is active (40k/autoloads/FactionAbilityManager.gd ~lines 462, 616, 812), and ChargePhase refuses a charge after an Advance without that flag (40k/phases/ChargePhase.gd ~2019-2041). The same text test is used in _should_unit_advance (AI-GAP-4, ~line 11549: 'has Advance and Charge - advancing allows charge' -> always Advance) and in _should_unit_advance_long_trip (RACE-1, ~line 11633: skips the 'enemy within charge reach' check), so it may also make Ork shooting units (Lootas, Burna Boyz, Tankbustas) Advance and lose their shooting. A legitimate advance-and-charge ability exists elsewhere (Custodes Blade Champion 'Swift Onslaught', while leading a unit): keep that working. Guardrails: Ork Advances toward objectives that were right or neutral (s7436 r3 Lootas Beta -5.25, s7438 r1 Lootas Gamma -2.75, s7437 r1 Lootas Alpha -0.58, s7438 r1 Beast Snagga +0.08) and s7442 r2 (a non-Ork Terminator Assault Squad attack advance, 0.0). This bug is in every bench game with Orks (Orks mirror and Custodes vs Orks fixtures), so a fix will fire there; think hard about full-game effects of Ork units Advancing less (slower to objectives in rounds 1-2, more charges, more shooting).

clusters.title: Round 1: a strong unit is sent back to capture our own home objective (often a second unit for it) instead of going forward
clusters.hint: Confirmed over 36 seeds with the V9 AI: s7468 r1 P1 (Custodes vs Orks): Custodian Guard Gamma 'moves toward obj_home_1 (capturing it (uncontrolled), obj 9.4 in away)' while Alpha is ALSO sent there; Gamma ADVANCING to obj_center instead: +6.86 [4.45, 9.27]. s7451 r1 P2 (Custodes mirror): Gamma makes a Normal move toward obj_center ('2 turns away', contest_race -13.74); ADVANCING there: +5.86 [3.09, 8.63] (Gamma's Guardian Spear is [ASSAULT], so Advancing costs no shooting; RACE-1's long-trip Advance test and _should_unit_advance may ignore [ASSAULT] - the reinforce_insurance designs found this too). Older confirmed findings of the same kind (round 2 sweeps, older AI; replay them to see what V9 does now): s7412 r1 P1 Beta 'Move obj_home_1 (capturing it (uncontrolled))' vs Advance obj_nml_1 +2.86 [1.27, 4.45]; s7411 r1 P1 Gamma 'Move obj_home_1 (capturing it (uncontrolled))' vs Advance obj_nml_1 +2.50 [0.71, 4.29].
